title: Transformer-only inference ASICs gain a first-class serving-stack backend by H1 2027
body: Etched came out of stealth on July 1 with a working transformer-specialized inference ASIC on TSMC's N4P, more than $1 billion in customer contracts signed before the part has shipped, and an architecture that hard-wires the transformer into silicon and shares one low-latency memory pool across the whole scale-up domain over a proprietary interconnect. The load-bearing move is not the funding but the architectural bet: dropping the training-oriented generality of a GPU to buy density on model serving, the workload that now dominates production spend. A fixed-function part only pays off if real model traffic can reach it without a bespoke integration for every deployment, and today the mainstream serving runtimes, vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM class stacks, are built around CUDA-style general accelerators with paged-attention and continuous-batching schedulers assuming a programmable GPU underneath. An order book measured in billions before first shipment is exactly the demand signal that pulls a serving stack to add a non-GPU, fixed-function transformer backend as a supported target rather than a fork. This also rhymes with the adjacent move of a rival accelerator vendor acquiring a CUDA-agnostic inference compiler to route models onto non-NVIDIA parts. Expect at least one mainstream open-source or hyperscaler-managed serving stack to expose a transformer-ASIC or comparable fixed-function inference backend as a documented, first-class deployment path, with the same model-definition and API surface a GPU target already gets, so that pointing production traffic at fixed-function silicon stops requiring a custom stack. The coupling is that a billion-dollar pre-ship order book turns backend generality from the ASIC vendor's private problem into a feature the serving layer ships.

reasoning.given: Mainstream serving runtimes assume programmable GPUs; a billion-dollar order book pulls in a fixed-function backend
reasoning.so_that: A mainstream serving stack exposes a transformer-ASIC fixed-function backend as a documented first-class deployment path
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; a serving runtime or managed stack lists a fixed-function transformer-ASIC backend
reasoning.plain_language: A chip that only runs transformers already has huge orders, so the software that serves AI models will add built-in support for that kind of chip.

summary: Etched left stealth with a working transformer-only inference ASIC and over $1B in contracts before shipping, betting on fixed-function density over GPU generality. Since mainstream serving runtimes assume programmable GPUs, expect at least one to expose a transformer-ASIC fixed-function backend as a first-class deployment path by H1 2027.
